working_title: Scotland's Ayrshire Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Turnberry, Prestwick, Royal Troon and Beyond
angle: Ayrshire is the most concentrated cluster of Open Championship links in the world, but most UK visitors either only book one marquee course or get priced out of the headline names entirely. This post maps the full circuit, from the flagship three down to the underrated alternatives, with honest practical guidance on access, visitor days, and how to build a realistic itinerary.
research_notes:
- Ayrshire's coastline southwest of Glasgow anchors three Open Championship venues: Prestwick (hosted 24 Opens, first in 1860), Royal Troon (hosted 9 Opens, most recently 2024 when Xander Schauffele won), and the Ailsa Course at Turnberry (hosted 4 Opens)
- Prestwick Golf Club was formally organised in 1851; designed with significant input from Old Tom Morris; some holes run alongside the railway line; closes to visitors on Saturdays (members only)
- Royal Troon offers visitor tee times on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays only; handicap certificate advisable; visitor fees in peak season reported in the £250–£350 range (treat as approximate, do not state as definitive current price)
- Turnberry: Ailsa Course is the flagship; Kintyre Course also available; resort hotel on site (Trump Turnberry); book well in advance
- Western Gailes: links course a few miles from Prestwick Airport; serves as an Open Qualifying venue when the Open is at Troon or Turnberry; a good-value alternative to the flagship trio
- Dundonald Links: North Ayrshire; described as a practical central base for multi-day trips; hosted the Women's Scottish Open in 2024 and 2025; clubhouse named 'Best in Scotland' in 2025 — good walkable option with more flexible visitor access
- Kilmarnock (Barassie) Golf Club: 27 holes of links golf just outside Troon; described as an 'if you know, you know' pick
- Prestwick St Nicholas Golf Club: separate club to Prestwick GC, founded 1851, often overlooked, links with views over the Ayrshire coast
- Gailes Links: another option in the corridor, cited by locals as good value
- Glasgow International Airport is the main gateway; drive to Troon/central Ayrshire coast approximately 40 minutes
- A hire car is essentially non-negotiable for an Ayrshire golf trip
- Buggies restricted to golfers with medical certificates at traditional links courses (walking expected)
- Troon town is the natural hub for most itineraries; Prestwick town described as an authentic golf-town base similar in feel to St Andrews but less crowded
- Ailsa Craig visible on clear days from several courses along the coast — a distinctive visual landmark worth noting for atmosphere
- Turnberry lighthouse walk a notable non-golf activity nearby
must_avoid:
- Do not state visitor green fees as definitive current prices; the £250–£350 figure is approximate and from third-party sources — describe as 'expect to pay premium rates, well into the hundreds of pounds at peak times' or similar general terms
- Do not fabricate any quotes from pros, reviewers, or course staff
- Do not imply personal first-hand experience of playing any of these courses unless the brief is updated with a human-supplied anecdote
- No betting or gambling content (e.g. odds on future Opens at these venues)
- No medical advice beyond noting that links courses expect visitors to walk (no buggies without a medical certificate)
- No em dashes anywhere in the post
- Ayrshire is not 'undiscovered' — do not use that framing; the angle is about navigating a well-known but logistically complex destination intelligently
- Northern Ireland's Causeway Coast post already covers Royal Portrush — do not conflate or cross-reference as a competing destination in a way that dilutes either post
